pattern.description: The chat transcript scrolls up as a conversation feed: the agent greeting exits off the top, the two user bubbles move up, the second bubble reflows to add 'please?' as the user finishes speaking, and an empty agent reply bubble fades in at the lower right, waiting for the answer.
pattern.why_premium: The transcript stays in lock-step with the voice: the word appears exactly as it is spoken, then the feed advances and pre-places an empty reply bubble, so the viewer anticipates the agent's answer before it is heard. Soft eased scroll and fade keep it calm rather than app-like.

build_hint.gsap: Thread container: gsap.to(thread, {y: '-=rowShift', duration: 0.5, ease: 'power2.inOut'}); first bubble also fades out as it crosses the top: gsap.to(greeting, {opacity: 0, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power1.in'}). Word append: gsap.from(pleaseWord, {opacity: 0, duration: 0.15}) with Flip on bubble2 for height growth. New reply bubble: gsap.fromTo(replyBubble, {opacity: 0, y: 24, scale: 0.96}, {opacity: 1, y: 0, scale: 1, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power3.out', delay: 0.2}).
build_hint.remotion: threadY = interpolate(spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 200}}), [0, 1], [0, -rowShift]); greeting opacity = interpolate(frame, [0, 9], [1, 0], {extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}); 'please?' shown when frame >= wordFrame with 4-frame opacity ramp; reply bubble uses spring({frame: frame - 6, fps, config: {damping: 200}}) for opacity, translateY 24->0 and scale 0.96->1.

notes: No fixed card mask is visible; the frame edge acts as the mask, so layout_reframe or a chat-feed pattern are plausible alternatives. b05, b10, b16 are vacated start positions of the second bubble and were not listed. Whether the reply bubble scales or only fades/slides is uncertain from the filmstrip.
